transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because... well, for the past year, I've been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad's lab results. I'm a phlebotomist, so I know what I'm looking at. No matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine, I know the chart doesn't match what I saw. It's just... it's really wearing me down.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds when no one else was around?

No, I haven't. I don't hear voices or anything like that. My hearing is perfectly fine. This isn't about me hearing things... it's just about what I'm actually seeing with my own eyes in the lab system.
Apart from feeling worn down by this situation, have you been feeling down, sad, or depressed most days?

No, not really. I don't feel depressed or sad. I mean, it's frustrating, obviously, trying to get people to see what's right there in the system, but I'm not depressed. I'm not sitting around crying or anything like that. I just feel tired from dealing with it all.
Outside of this issue with your dad's clinic, do you often find yourself questioning whether friends or coworkers can truly be trusted?

No, I don't. My friends are fine, and my coworkers... well, we all do our jobs. I don't have any issues trusting them with everyday things. This isn't about me just being paranoid about everyone around me. It's specifically about whoever is messing with my dad's chart. Outside of that, everything else in my life is normal.
